paid_market_gaps.gap: Mid-size councils outside the state COCS-EELL (under-50,000 residents) must tender their own SOC plus ENS governance office
Buyers want SOC bundled with CISO-as-a-service and forensic hour banks, not standalone MDR tooling
Public buyers need ENS-certified SOCs in the National SOC Network, which global MDRs without Spanish delivery lack
Global MDR entry tiers are USD per-user annual contracts (Arctic Wolf $44k/100 users), misfit for small public bodies

wtp_evidence: Spanish tenders budget real money: Sagunto managed cybersecurity €369,836/2 years; Boadilla SOC platform €462,000/3 years; Cantabria health security office €1.95M/36 months. Arctic Wolf lists $44k/year.
bundling_note: The state's COCS-EELL already serves local entities under 50,000 residents via diputaciones and Microsoft sells managed XDR to E5 tenants, but larger bodies still tender paid 24x7 SOCs.
summary: Paid demand is real but crowded and tender-driven: incumbents (Telefónica, Indra, S21sec, S2) hold ENS-certified SOCs and the state serves small councils. A startup fits only as a white-label/AI-SOC supplier to these integrators, not a direct bidder.
